create.name: Sakya Künga Chöling
create.bio:
Sakya Künga Chöling is a Tibetan Buddhist centre of the Sakya school in Trieste, in north-eastern Italy, and the first Buddhist centre to be founded in the region of Friuli Venezia Giulia. It was established by the Tibetan master Khenchen Sherab Gyaltsen Amipa Rinpoche, and since his death its spiritual guide has been his chosen successor, Khenpo Tashi Sangpo Amipa, who oversees all the Sakya centres Khenchen Sherab founded across Europe. A Sakya nun, Ani Sherab Choden, lives at the centre and serves as its president; before taking robes she sang professionally in Trieste's opera house. The shrine room, in a city flat on Via Marconi, is hung with painted thangkas around a richly laid altar.

Every Wednesday evening Ani Sherab Choden leads teaching and guided meditation in person, and a second weekly session of practice and teaching takes place on Zoom for those who register. Members also gather regularly for Tara and Mahakala practices, study traditional Sakya texts, and follow an introductory course for newcomers. Alongside its Dharma activity, the centre runs a long-standing project supporting Tibetan refugee children in India and Nepal through sponsorship and study grants, and the community of around a hundred members and friends meets each December for a seasonal gathering.
